title: The ruled cubic passes local torsion but fails global normalization proportionality
content: Let X_p be the ruled cubic p=xz^2-y^2w=0 containing the rational quartic C. Its singular locus is the line y=z=0, and C meets this line at its two endpoints, which are the pinch points. Thus the local APic groups along C are Z/2 and the local torsion condition is compatible with STCI. On the normalization S isomorphic to Bl_P(P^2), with class notation (a,b)=a l-b e, the hyperplane, conductor preimage, and lifted quartic have classes H=(2,1), Gamma=(1,0), and C-tilde=(2,0). The last class is the strict transform of a conic avoiding P. The equation r(2,0)=m(2,1) has no positive solution, so the necessary proportionality already fails in Pic(S), and hence C is not an STCI on X_p.
significance: Gives a failure mode complementary to the cuspidal cone: local singularity torsion is not sufficient when the global class on the normalization is wrong.
assumptions: The base field is algebraically closed of characteristic zero
The ruled cubic normalization and class notation are as in Hartshorne-Polini
source_material: Hartshorne-Polini, Example 5.7(b) of Quasi-cyclic modules and Examples 6.3 and 7.12 of Divisor class groups

relations.explanation: Computes the APic obstruction on a ruled cubic containing the quartic.
Both eliminate explicit singular cubic surfaces, but at different stages of the normalization-conductor analysis.
Shows that local torsion and global normalization proportionality must be tested separately.

provenance.objective: Determine whether the rational quartic can become proportional to a hyperplane in APic of a second singular cubic surface.
provenance.method: Compute the singular line, identify the normalization class of the lifted curve, and test proportionality to the hyperplane class.
provenance.reasoning_summary: Pinch-point torsion removes the local obstruction, but the independent Picard coordinates on the cubic scroll make global proportionality impossible.
